To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the anabolic fate and the catabolic fate of AA in the liver are regulated in a different way and are influenced by the nature of nutrients provided to the liver, the hormonal status of the animal and the nutritional/physiological status of the animal.
the anabolic fate (protein synthesis) or the catabolic fate (protein oxidation and gluconeogenesis) of AA is dependent on the nutritional state of the animal.
the liver plays a key role in the partitioning of AA among tissues and that the fates of these nutrients are highly regulated.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the mechanisms involved in regulating AA metabolism within the liver in response to nutrient availability and body requirements, with a particular focus on the role of the liver in AA metabolism during lactation and growth.
the regulation of the anabolism of AA within the liver and the underlying mechanisms.
the nutritional regulation of the fate of AA within the liver, and the underlying mechanisms involved in the control of AA utilisation by the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fates of amino acids are regulated by nutritional parameters, but the mechanisms involved are highly species-specific and depend upon the physiological state.
nutritional regulation of AA metabolism within the liver is complex, but that the liver is capable of adapting its metabolic pathways in response to nutrient supply.
nutritional parameters are the main drivers of AA metabolism within the liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liver has the ability to respond rapidly to the nutritional requirements of the organism, but also to adapt to other physiological states (growth, lactation, etc.).
the liver is an organ with high plasticity in AA metabolism, which can respond to the nutritional requirements of the body, but also to other physiological and/or pathological conditions.
the fates of the AA are mainly regulated by nutritional factors, and that the liver is a major organ involved in the regulation of the anabolism of AA in the whole body.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver is a key organ in the nutritional regulation of AA utilisation.
the liver is a key organ in the control of AA utilisation and partitioning in the body, and its function is finely tuned to the nutritional status of the organism.
AA oxidation and protein synthesis are highly dependent on the availability of AA, whereas the synthesis of acute-phase proteins and gluconeogenesis are less so.
